origin.description: Encode a raw vector, a file name, or a binary connection as base64 text.

arguments.name: what
arguments.text: A raw vector, a binary connection, or a file name. A character string is opened as a file, not encoded as text.

arguments.name: linewidth
arguments.text: Maximum characters on a line. Zero or NA means no limit. Values from 1 to 3 are treated as 4, and the width is then rounded down to a multiple of 4.

arguments.name: newline
arguments.text: Used only when linewidth is set. A string joins the lines into one string. If it is omitted, each line is its own element.

origin.details: An empty raw vector is character(0). An empty file is NULL when the lines stay separate, and an empty string when they are pasted. A file is read in slices of 65535 bytes, grown so each slice spans whole lines.
origin.value: A character vector. One string when there is no line limit or newline is set, otherwise one element per line.
origin.example:
base64encode(1:100)
base64encode(1:100, 70)
base64encode(1:100, 70, "\n")
x <- charToRaw("the decoded content, otherwise the number of bytes")
y <- base64decode(base64encode(x))
stopifnot(identical(x, y))

translation.description: Encode bytes, numbers, a binary file object, or a file name as base64 text.

arguments.name: what
arguments.text: Bytes, a list or range of numbers, a binary file object, or a file name. A string is a path. None is an empty raw vector.

arguments.name: linewidth
arguments.text: Maximum characters on a line. None, a non-number, an empty list, or a missing value means no limit. 1, 2, and 3 become 4, then the width is rounded down to a multiple of 4.

arguments.name: newline
arguments.text: None leaves the lines separate. A string, including the empty string, joins them. The first string is used. A missing string there is the letters NA on a raw vector.

translation.details: An empty raw vector is []. An empty file is None when linewidth is positive and newline is None, and [""] otherwise. A file longer than 65535 bytes is encoded in slices, and a newline is pasted between those slices even when linewidth is unset.
translation.value: A list of strings. One string when there is no line limit or newline is set, otherwise one string per line. None is the empty-file line split.
translation.example:
from base64enc.base64encode import base64encode
print(base64encode(list(range(1, 101))))
print(base64encode(list(range(1, 101)), 70))
print(base64encode(list(range(1, 101)), 70, "\n"))
